trust_decision.summary: The package owns the whole decision: every string handed to its single public function must be decoded as far as possible in time bounded by input length, and that bound is enforced inside its own fallback decoder, not at any caller.

landing_point.why: The report says 'exponential decoding of malformed percent-encoded input'; the only retry/re-decode machinery is the fallback `decode` entered from the native-decode `catch` (index.js:83-89), whose loop at index.js:32-36 re-invokes the divide-and-conquer helper `decodeComponents` (index.js:5-24) for every split index.

fix_sites.module_kind: package root module, ESM library entry (no framework/handler layer)
package root module, ESM library entry (no framework/handler layer)
package root module (cosmetic: TypeError message rebuilt as a template literal, same rendered text)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory's exponential time is produced by the recursive helper `decodeComponents`; once that recursion is replaced by a single scan, the remaining work in `customDecodeURIComponent` is plain native string replacement over already-decoded chunks, so it can be argued to be a different mechanism the advisory never described.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The package's documented lossy behaviour must survive any rewrite: BOM pairs decode to two U+FFFD (index.js:45-46), a bare `%C2` sentinel decodes to one U+FFFD (index.js:66, readme.md:48-49 use it as a regression), and undecodable bytes stay literal (test.js:21 `'%ab'` -> `'%ab'`). A length cap or strict-reject 'fix' also breaks long but perfectly valid input that the native fast path handles today (index.js:83-85).

O6_input_shapes: truncated multi-byte sequence at end of run (`%F0%9F`, `%E2%82`, `%C3`)
non-continuation byte in the middle of a multi-byte run (`%F0%9F%41`, `%F0%41%82%83`)
invalid / overlong lead bytes (0xC0, 0xC1, 0xF5-0xFF) and orphaned continuation bytes (0x80-0xBF)
structurally valid but semantically invalid sequences (overlong `%E0%80%80`, surrogate `%ED%A0%80`, >U+10FFFF `%F4%90%80%80`)
invalid hex syntax (`%G0`, `%0G`, `foo%bar`, `%u0041`) and lone `%` used as a run separator
hex digit case variants (`%c3%a5` / `%C3%a5`) and repeated BOM pairs in context
non-string values of every typeof (TypeError path)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Per-distinct-run whole-string respend: `customDecodeURIComponent` keys its replaceMap by every distinct malformed run found by `multiMatcher` and then runs one `input.replace(/<key>/g, ...)` over the entire input per key, so time grows with (distinct runs x input length) even after `decode` becomes a single scan.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is not recursive and it is native `String.replace`; a solver can call it bounded/linear-by-construction and treat only `decode`/`decodeComponents` as the reported flaw - and the published fix leaves this block untouched (only a comment is added, fix.diff:155).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function that calls the fixed decoder, 30 lines below the landing point, same file

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second decoder implementation kept beside `decode` (e.g. a `decodeAll`/recursive helper or an option-bearing `decodeUriComponent(input, {maxSplit})`) that re-implements the divide-and-conquer split instead of delegating to the fixed scanner.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The pre-fix code already shipped two decoder paths (`decode` and `customDecodeURIComponent`); a maintainer adding an option or a second exported helper would naturally copy the existing split logic.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A dual-build sibling `index.cjs` (or `dist/index.js`) for CommonJS consumers, containing a verbatim copy of the old recursive decoder.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The package is ESM-only with `engines: node >=14.16`; adding a CJS build for older bundlers/Node is the standard npm interop move, and a copy-paste build step is how it is usually done.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Cap the recursion depth or the split loop (or add an input-length limit) in `decode`, or catch the blow-up and return the input unchanged, which stops the slow case while preserving the visible small-string examples.

out_of_scope_notes: index.js:72 passes a decoded value straight as the replacement string to String.replace, so `$&`/`$1` patterns inside a decoded run are expanded - a compatibility/correctness quirk, not part of this DoS advisory, not pursued.
index.js:72 also builds `new RegExp(key, 'g')` from an input-derived key; keys are restricted to `%`+hex by the matchers, so this is not a regex-injection route, noted only to close it off.
